name: First marathon
summary: Train for a first marathon with a 16 to 20-week plan of long runs, cutback weeks and a taper.

onboarding.reaction: That's the big one. We'll count back from race day.

onboarding.prompt: About how many miles a week are you running now?
onboarding.reaction: Whatever the number, that's your base.

onboarding.prompt: Any injuries or niggles we should plan around?
onboarding.reaction: Thanks for flagging it. Check it with your doctor or physio before the build.

onboarding.prompt: Which day works for long runs?
onboarding.reaction: Long-run day set. Everything else fits around it.

onboarding.prompt: How many runs a week can you fit?
onboarding.reaction: Good. Quality beats quantity on a first marathon.

onboarding.prompt: Tap your free running slots, including the long-run window.
onboarding.reaction: Calendar holds placed. Long runs get the biggest block.

phases.name: Base
benchmarks: Run the planned days for 4 of 6 weeks
Long run reaches about 10 miles or 16 km
actions: Cutback week every third or fourth week

phases.name: Build
benchmarks: Long run reaches 16 to 18 miles or 26 to 29 km
Practice race-day fuel and kit on long runs
actions: One steady or tempo run a week
Long run on the chosen day

phases.name: Taper and race
benchmarks: Mileage steps down over 2 to 3 weeks
actions: Race-week checklist: kit, route, fuel, sleep

plan_blueprint.calendar: Runs on the chosen slots, the long run on the chosen day, cutback weeks marked, taper weeks shaded lighter, and race day as an all-day event. Plan length (16 to 20 weeks) is set from the race date and current miles.

approach_variants.habit: Same days and times every week; streak counts weeks with all planned runs done.
approach_variants.willpower: Long-run countdown and peak-week challenge; partners can send a dare for the toughest long run.
approach_variants.time: Every run, stretch and foam-roll session is a calendar block; weekly hours review.
approach_variants.reward: Owner-picked rewards at the first 13-mile run, the peak long run and the finish line.
approach_variants.resource: Opening week sorts shoes, fuel to test, a long-run route, and a running club or buddy.

guardrails: Talk to your doctor before starting. GoalKin offers education, not medical advice.
Pain that changes how you run means rest and get it checked; the plan will wait.
Extra care on hot days: slow down, drink water and shorten the run if needed.
Every plan item can be edited, moved or removed, and you can add your own steps.
Product, app or recipe ideas are labeled as suggestions; any affiliate link is disclosed.
restart_rules: A missed easy run is dropped. A missed long run moves to the next free day that week, or the week repeats. Missing 10 days or more triggers a re-plan with a cutback week first; if the race date gets too close, the plan suggests a later race or a shorter distance.
